title: Low-degree long exact Tor sequence in the first variable, natural in the second
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $0\to Q\xrightarrow{u}Q'\xrightarrow{v}Q''\to0$ a short exact sequence of $R$-modules and $N$ an $R$-module. Then there is an $R$-linear map $\delta_N:\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(Q'',N)\to Q\otimes_RN$ such that the sequence $$\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(Q',N)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tor}_1(v,N)}\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(Q'',N)\xrightarrow{\delta_N}Q\otimes_RN\xrightarrow{u\otimes1}Q'\otimes_RN\xrightarrow{v\otimes1}Q''\otimes_RN\to0$$ is exact (with $\operatorname{Tor}$ and its functoriality as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]), and $\delta$ is natural in $N$: for every $R$-linear map $g:N\to N'$ one has $(1_Q\otimes g)\circ\delta_N=\delta_{N'}\circ\operatorname{Tor}_1(Q'',g)$, so that all maps of the sequence commute with the maps induced by $g$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M0 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-tor, line 18291: the sequence for a short exact sequence in the second variable) together with Lemma Tag 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right, line 18534: Tor_i(M, N) = Tor_i(N, M)), which give it in the first variable; used in this form in More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 0912 (more-algebra.tex lines 6515--6520). Tags verified in tags/tags: 00M0,algebra-lemma-long-exact-sequence-tor; 00M3,algebra-lemma-tor-left-right

proof.text: Resolutions. By [lem-weil-pbc-free-resolution-ses-split] choose chain complexes of free $R$-modules $F_\bullet,F'_\bullet,F''_\bullet$ with augmentations $\varepsilon:F_0\to Q$, $\varepsilon':F'_0\to Q'$, $\varepsilon'':F''_0\to Q''$ making them free resolutions of $Q,Q',Q''$, morphisms of complexes $\alpha:F_\bullet\to F'_\bullet$, $\beta:F'_\bullet\to F''_\bullet$ with $\varepsilon'\alpha_0=u\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon''\beta_0=v\varepsilon'$, and maps $\pi_n:F'_n\to F_n$, $s_n:F''_n\to F'_n$ with $\beta_n\alpha_n=0$, $\pi_n\alpha_n=1$, $\beta_ns_n=1$, $\alpha_n\pi_n+s_n\beta_n=1$. These choices depend only on the short exact sequence, not on $N$; they are fixed for the rest of the proof and for all modules $N$ at once (this is what makes $\delta$ below natural in $N$).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 065P (lemma-reverse-long-exact-seq-ext, lines 17681--17711), transposed from Hom_R(-, N) to - (x)_R N

proof.text: Tensoring with $N$. For an $R$-module $N$ put $C_\bullet=F_\bullet\otimes_RN$, $C'_\bullet=F'_\bullet\otimes_RN$, $C''_\bullet=F''_\bullet\otimes_RN$ (differentials $d\otimes1$ etc.) and $a=\alpha\otimes1_N:C_\bullet\to C'_\bullet$, $b=\beta\otimes1_N:C'_\bullet\to C''_\bullet$; these are morphisms of complexes since $-\otimes1_N$ preserves composites. For every $n$ the sequence $0\to C_n\xrightarrow{a_n}C'_n\xrightarrow{b_n}C''_n\to0$ is exact: applying $-\otimes1_N$ (which preserves composites, identities and sums of maps) to the identities of Step 1 gives $b_na_n=0$, $(\pi_n\otimes1)a_n=1$, $b_n(s_n\otimes1)=1$ and $a_n(\pi_n\otimes1)+(s_n\otimes1)b_n=1$; so $a_n$ is injective, $b_n$ is surjective, and if $b_n(x)=0$ then $x=a_n((\pi_n\otimes1)x)$. For an $R$-linear $g:N\to N'$ write $C_\bullet(g)=1_{F_\bullet}\otimes g:C_\bullet\to F_\bullet\otimes_RN'$, and likewise $C'_\bullet(g)$, $C''_\bullet(g)$; these are morphisms of complexes commuting with $a$ and $b$, since $(\alpha_n\otimes1_{N'})(1\otimes g)=\alpha_n\otimes g=(1\otimes g)(\alpha_n\otimes1_N)$ and likewise for $\beta$ and the differentials.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 065P (lemma-reverse-long-exact-seq-ext, lines 17681--17711), transposed from Hom_R(-, N) to - (x)_R N

proof.text: Identifications. By [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], applied with the free (hence projective) resolutions of Step 1, there are isomorphisms $\iota_N:\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(Q,N)\to H_1(C_\bullet)$, $\iota'_N:\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(Q',N)\to H_1(C'_\bullet)$, $\iota''_N:\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(Q'',N)\to H_1(C''_\bullet)$, where $H_1=\ker(d_1\otimes1)/\operatorname{im}(d_2\otimes1)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tor-map-via-resolution-lift] (1), applied to $\varphi=v$ and the lift $\beta$ ($\varepsilon''\beta_0=v\varepsilon'$), $\iota''_N\circ\operatorname{Tor}_1(v,N)=H_1(b)\circ\iota'_N$; by [lem-weil-pbc-tor-map-via-resolution-lift] (2), applied to $g:N\to N'$ and the resolution $F''_\bullet$, $\iota''_{N'}\circ\operatorname{Tor}_1(Q'',g)=H_1(C''_\bullet(g))\circ\iota''_N$. In degree $0$: $F_1\xrightarrow{d_1}F_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}Q\to0$ is exact, so by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] $F_1\otimes N\xrightarrow{d_1\otimes1}F_0\otimes N\xrightarrow{\varepsilon\otimes1}Q\otimes N\to0$ is exact, and $\varepsilon\otimes1$ induces an isomorphism $c_N:H_0(C_\bullet)=\operatorname{coker}(d_1\otimes1_N)\to Q\otimes_RN$; likewise $c'_N:H_0(C'_\bullet)\to Q'\otimes_RN$. Since $(\varepsilon'\otimes1)(\alpha_0\otimes1)=(u\otimes1)(\varepsilon\otimes1)$ one has $c'_N\circ H_0(a)=(u\otimes1_N)\circ c_N$, and since $(\varepsilon\otimes1_{N'})(1_{F_0}\otimes g)=(1_Q\otimes g)(\varepsilon\otimes1_N)$ one has $c_{N'}\circ H_0(C_\bullet(g))=(1_Q\otimes g)\circ c_N$.

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00LY (lines 18205--18290): Tor computed from a free resolution of the first variable, functoriality via Lemma 00LZ; Lemma Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact) for degree 0

proof.text: The connecting map. Write $Z_1(C)=\ker(d_1\otimes1)$, $B_1(C)=\operatorname{im}(d_2\otimes1)$ and $\bar C_1=C_1/B_1(C)$, likewise for $C',C''$. Consider the commutative diagram with rows $\bar C_1\xrightarrow{\bar a_1}\bar C'_1\xrightarrow{\bar b_1}\bar C''_1\to0$ and $0\to C_0\xrightarrow{a_0}C'_0\xrightarrow{b_0}C''_0$ and vertical maps $\bar d_1,\bar d'_1,\bar d''_1$ induced by the differentials (well defined as $d_1d_2=0$; the squares commute since $a,b$ are morphisms of complexes). The bottom row is exact by Step 2. The top row is exact: $\bar b_1$ is surjective as $b_1$ is; $\bar b_1\bar a_1=0$ as $b_1a_1=0$; if $y\in C'_1$ has $b_1(y)\in B_1(C'')$, say $b_1(y)=d''_2(z'')$, write $z''=b_2(z')$ ($b_2$ surjective), then $b_1(y-d'_2z')=b_1(y)-d''_2b_2(z')=0$, so $y-d'_2z'=a_1(x)$ for some $x\in C_1$ by Step 2, and the class of $y$ is $\bar a_1$ of the class of $x$. The kernels of the vertical maps are $\ker\bar d_1=Z_1(C)/B_1(C)=H_1(C_\bullet)$ (and likewise for $C',C''$) and the cokernels are $\operatorname{coker}\bar d_1=C_0/\operatorname{im}d_1=H_0(C_\bullet)$; the maps induced by $\bar a_1,\bar b_1,a_0,b_0$ are $H_1(a),H_1(b),H_0(a),H_0(b)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-modules] there is an $R$-linear $\partial_N:H_1(C''_\bullet)\to H_0(C_\bullet)$ with $H_1(C'_\bullet)\xrightarrow{H_1(b)}H_1(C''_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\partial_N}H_0(C_\bullet)\xrightarrow{H_0(a)}H_0(C'_\bullet)$ exact, given by: for a cycle $z\in Z_1(C'')$ choose $y\in C'_1$ with $b_1(y)=z$ and $w\in C_0$ with $a_0(w)=d'_1(y)$; then $\partial_N[z]=[w]$.

proof.text: Exactness. Put $\delta_N=c_N\circ\partial_N\circ\iota''_N:\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(Q'',N)\to Q\otimes_RN$, an $R$-linear map. Under the isomorphisms $\iota'_N,\iota''_N,c_N,c'_N$ the part $\operatorname{Tor}_1(Q',N)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Tor}_1(v,N)}\operatorname{Tor}_1(Q'',N)\xrightarrow{\delta_N}Q\otimes N\xrightarrow{u\otimes1}Q'\otimes N$ of the claimed sequence corresponds, by Step 3 ($\iota''_N\operatorname{Tor}_1(v,N)=H_1(b)\iota'_N$, $c'_NH_0(a)=(u\otimes1)c_N$, and $\delta_N\iota''^{-1}_N=c_N\partial_N$ by definition), to the exact sequence $H_1(C')\xrightarrow{H_1(b)}H_1(C'')\xrightarrow{\partial_N}H_0(C)\xrightarrow{H_0(a)}H_0(C')$ of Step 4; a sequence isomorphic to an exact one is exact, so the claimed sequence is exact at $\operatorname{Tor}_1(Q'',N)$ and at $Q\otimes N$. Exactness at $Q'\otimes N$ and surjectivity of $v\otimes1$: [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] applied to $Q\xrightarrow{u}Q'\xrightarrow{v}Q''\to0$.

source.place: Homology, Lemma Tag 0111 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-chain, lines 2967--3007): the maps come from the snake lemma (Tag 010H) applied to the diagram of the A_i/Im(d_{i+1}) -> Ker(d_{i-1})

proof.text: Naturality in $N$. Let $g:N\to N'$ be $R$-linear and $z\in Z_1(C'')$ (for $N$). Choose $y,w$ as in Step 4, so $b_1(y)=z$, $a_0(w)=d'_1(y)$, $\partial_N[z]=[w]$. By Step 2 the maps $C(g),C'(g),C''(g)$ commute with $a,b$ and the differentials, so $C''_1(g)z$ is a cycle for $N'$, $b_1(C'_1(g)y)=C''_1(g)z$ and $a_0(C_0(g)w)=d'_1(C'_1(g)y)$; these are admissible choices in the formula of [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-modules] (whose value does not depend on the choices), so $\partial_{N'}H_1(C''(g))[z]=[C_0(g)w]=H_0(C(g))\partial_N[z]$. Hence, using Step 3 ($\iota''_{N'}\operatorname{Tor}_1(Q'',g)=H_1(C''(g))\iota''_N$ and $c_{N'}H_0(C(g))=(1_Q\otimes g)c_N$): $\delta_{N'}\circ\operatorname{Tor}_1(Q'',g)=c_{N'}\partial_{N'}H_1(C''(g))\iota''_N=c_{N'}H_0(C(g))\partial_N\iota''_N=(1_Q\otimes g)c_N\partial_N\iota''_N=(1_Q\otimes g)\circ\delta_N$. The other squares commute by bifunctoriality: $(1\otimes g)(u\otimes1)=(u\otimes1)(1\otimes g)$ and $(1\otimes g)(v\otimes1)=(v\otimes1)(1\otimes g)$ on elements $q\otimes x$; and $\operatorname{Tor}_1(Q'',g)\operatorname{Tor}_1(v,N)=\operatorname{Tor}_1(v,N')\operatorname{Tor}_1(Q',g)$ because by Step 3 both sides correspond under $\iota'_N,\iota''_{N'}$ to $H_1(\beta\otimes g)=H_1(C''(g))H_1(b)=H_1(b)H_1(C'(g))$ (using [lem-weil-pbc-tor-map-via-resolution-lift] (1) for $N'$ and (2) for $F'_\bullet$).
